context.process_name: Due From Funds & Portfolio Companies Billing
context.objective: Document how we carry out Due From Funds & Portfolio Companies Billing, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Oh, well, nothing dramatic starts it, honestly. Nobody emails us to say go. It is just the internal close calendar, at the end of each billing period, which for this client, One Rock, is quarterly, and it always lands right on top of month-end when everybody is already drowning. I swear month-end is designed by someone who hates accountants. Anyway, the fund side goes first, it follows the upstream source package and it is less complicated, and the portfolio company billing usually comes after. Before I really begin I make sure the Sage receivable activity for the period is there, the prior approved workbooks, the support in Box, the client Expense Tracker, the customer parent fields in Sage AR, and that the reviewer and client collaboration channels are available. My cousin once started baking a wedding cake before checking she had eggs, total disaster, and that is exactly how I think about this. Then the first real thing I do, as the preparer, is record the billing period and populations, copy last period's fund workbook and portfolio company workbook into the current cycle location, update the period references, including the transaction report header on all the roughly 25 to 27 portfolio tabs, and confirm fund tabs, affiliate tabs, portfolio tabs, the Notes tab, formulas and pivots are all there. If an entity is missing or extra, I confirm the population before loading any data.
Once the population is confirmed, how do you load the period’s data into the workbooks?

Right, so for the fund side, I run the Sage general ledger for accounts 1101 through 1105, the full billing period, with the location filter. I export it to Excel and honestly the export is ugly, I have to wrap text and strip out all the merge and center formatting. Whoever designed that report layout, I would like a word. Then I add a net column, debit minus credit, fill it down through every account section, paste it as values, and only then delete the original debit and credit columns. Next I remove every row where the document number starts with Invoice, because those are prior invoices and you would bill them twice otherwise. Then I sum what is left by account and compare it to the Sage ending balance. If there is any difference at all, I stop, I do not populate the fund tabs. Reminds me of my old car, the fuel gauge was off by a quarter tank and I ignored it once, never again. Once it ties, I add blank rows to each fund tab, copy transaction dates through net amount, not the Sage running balances, remove unused rows, extend the running balance and sum formulas, and check each tab agrees to its Per Sage amount. I never force a tie with an unexplained manual entry. I leave the GL coding column blank for the internal fund team and mark the finished account sections in my source file so nothing gets processed twice. Affiliates come after that.
How do you handle the affiliate billing after the fund account sections are complete?

Affiliates, yes. So I pull the whole Due From Affiliates account out of Sage with no customer filter, and clean it the same way as the fund export, net column, values, prior Invoice rows out. Then I build a pivot, Customer Name in the rows, Transaction Amount as the values. I exclude the GP entities, old funds we no longer bill, and anything out of population, but only under confirmed population rules, I do not just decide that myself. Then I populate each affiliate tab. And here is the bit people skip when it is month-end and the coffee machine is broken again, which it was all of last quarter by the way: I run a separate Sage report for every single affiliate and check the tab agrees with it. The grouped report alone is not good enough because it can miss backdated entries. If the grouped and the individual differ, I use the individual one to investigate, document it, and the reviewer decides, and that tab stays open until it is resolved. After that I gather support: sort by document number, pull invoice PDFs and allocation support from the vendor folders in Box, journal support from Sage or email, credits and refunds from email, all into one consolidated cycle folder, cross-referenced to the workbook lines. If backup is missing I have to find it before anything gets submitted. My neighbour keeps receipts in a shoebox, drives me mad.
Who receives the consolidated billing package when it is submitted?

It goes through a chain, it is not one person. First our own reviewer looks at the Sage reconciliations and any unusual items or missing support. They do not re-review the vendor invoice support itself, because those invoices already had two approvals in Mineral Tree upstream. Then the internal fund team reviews the package, fills in the general ledger coding I left blank, and writes their questions on the Notes tab. I resolve those notes and send questions to the client where needed. Then I put the package in the Client Collaboration folder and notify One Rock. They send feedback by email, I record it, update the workbook, and we go round again until they give final approval. If their feedback changes an amount I redo all the reconciliations and get approval again, every time, which at month-end feels like painting a bridge. My uncle actually painted bridges, said you never finish. How fast they have to turn it around, or the exact wording of final approval, I honestly do not know, nobody has ever told me. After approval I create the AR invoices in Sage, either updating a prior invoice or by an approved bulk import, dated the first of the month after period end, reference quarter and year with the memo matching. I print and save each one by entity name, invoice number and amount, they get an internal review, then go to the fund team, who send the payment request to Treasury. We ask for copies of the payment notifications so cash can be matched.
What does this billing work ultimately provide to One Rock?

In the end One Rock gets approved, reconciled workbooks, printed invoices for the funds, affiliates and portfolio companies, the per-company deal team files and an updated Expense Tracker. But we have not covered the portfolio company half, and that is the monster. I pull Sage account 1201 for the quarter, no customer or location filter, clean it like before, plus drop the department column and the 1201 summary header row, take out prior Invoice rows, pivot by customer, and exclude approved write-offs, supported, never just deleted. Then for every add-on I check the parent in Sage AR and combine it with the parent tab, paste rows in, refresh the expense type pivot, and tie each tab to its own individual Sage report. Do Not Bill items stay in the detail so it ties to Sage but come out of the billable total. Who approves a Do Not Bill, I do not know. Same review chain, then one Excel per company, current quarter only, for the deal teams. Then I update the Expense Tracker and tie the net to Sage. Accrued balance versus credit, I still need One Rock to confirm what they mean. Last, I group classes into Professional Fees, Other Expenses, Meals and Travel, bulk import, check each invoice is one page. If the entity is reserve funded, the invoice goes straight to Treasury, otherwise the normal payment chain. My dentist bills faster than this, honestly, month-end or not.
What does One Rock need to clarify about the accrued balance versus credit in the Expense Tracker?
This capture still has open sections. 14 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.
